profile_text.body:
Glean is a for-profit enterprise AI company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its platform is designed to connect to a company's internal data and enable employees to search for information, generate content, and automate workflows across the organization. The company describes its approach as built for enterprise from the start, emphasizing that its system is permission-aware, secure, and explainable, with over 100 connectors to various data sources and controls around data access governance.

Glean's core product, also called Glean, sits in the enterprise AI platforms and agent orchestration category, combining knowledge search with an AI assistant and the ability to build and deploy agents. The company cites deployments at Booking.com, where it became the first AI platform adopted company-wide, at Ericsson, which uses it to open enterprise data and let teams build agents, at GCash, where it serves as a centralized searchable intranet with agent-building capabilities, and at Zillow, where the company reports an 80 percent adoption rate. Zillow is quoted describing Glean as going beyond enterprise search by allowing teams to leverage all their data through the latest AI models.

The site's held facts note 161 California legal exposure entries, though no specific cases are on record. Glean also has a presence in the MCP registry through a server listed as co.gleanit/gleanit, which supports searching, reading, and writing highlights, notes, screenshots, collections, projects, and tags within the Gleanit application.
